title: Substances that boost performance

draft.title: Substances that boost performance
card: Some athletes take substances to improve performance. Many are banned in sport by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), and in Australia Sport Integrity Australia helps enforce the rules.
Anabolic steroids
These are drugs similar to the male hormone testosterone. They help the body build muscle and recover faster, so they can increase strength and power.
Health risks
Steroid use can cause liver damage, heart problems, acne, mood swings and aggression. It can also disrupt the body's natural hormones.
Banned
Anabolic steroids are on the banned list because they give an unfair advantage and risk harm. An athlete who tests positive can face a ban from competing.
draft.remember: Steroids can build muscle, but they carry health risks and are banned.

a.q: Why do some athletes take anabolic steroids?
opts: To build muscle and recover faster
To lower their heart rate under pressure
To raise the oxygen carried in their blood
To calm nerves before a skills event
a.why: Anabolic steroids help the body build muscle and recover, which can increase strength and power. Lowering heart rate is the aim of beta blockers, not steroids, and the card does not link steroids to oxygen carrying.
a.clue: Think about what 'anabolic' drugs help the body build.

b.q: Jess, a shot putter in Ballarat, tests positive for anabolic steroids. She says they only helped her train harder and did not harm her. Why is she still in breach of the rules?
opts: Steroids are banned, whatever the effect on her
Steroids are only banned if they cause harm
Steroids are banned only at national events
Steroids are allowed if used to recover from training
b.why: Anabolic steroids are on the banned list because they give an unfair advantage and risk health. Whether Jess feels harmed does not change this. The ban applies to the substance itself, not to how it affected one athlete.
b.clue: The ban is on the substance, not on the result for one person.

a.best: To build muscle and recover faster

b.best: Steroids are banned, whatever the effect on her

problems.detail: The clue ('Think about what anabolic drugs help the body build') nearly gives the answer away by pointing straight to the only option containing 'build'.
Why (a) explains beta blockers (lowering heart rate), a term that belongs to point 2 of the chapter. The distractors also draw on EPO and beta blockers, which this card does not teach.
The clue ('The ban is on the substance, not on the result for one person') restates the right option, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts are accurate and both questions have one clear right answer. However, both clues nearly give the answers away, and why (a) explains beta blockers, which belong to point 2.

proposal.title: Substances that boost performance
card: Some athletes take substances to improve performance. Many are banned in sport by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), and in Australia Sport Integrity Australia helps enforce the rules.
Anabolic steroids
These are drugs similar to the male hormone testosterone. They help the body build muscle and recover faster, so they can increase strength and power.
Health risks
Steroid use can cause liver damage, heart problems, acne, mood swings and aggression. It can also disrupt the body's natural hormones.
Banned
Anabolic steroids are banned both in and out of competition, because they give an unfair advantage and risk harm. An athlete who tests positive can face a ban from competing.
proposal.remember: Steroids can build muscle, but they carry health risks and are banned.

a.q: Which statement about anabolic steroids is correct?
opts: They build muscle, but they are banned in sport
They build muscle, and they are allowed in sport
They are banned, but they carry no health risks
They copy a natural hormone, so they are safe to use
a.why: Steroids can build muscle and strength, yet they are banned because they give an unfair advantage and risk harm. Being similar to testosterone does not make them safe: they can damage the liver and heart and disrupt natural hormones.
a.clue: Check each half of the statement against the card.

b.q: Jess, a shot putter in Ballarat, tests positive for anabolic steroids. She says they only helped her train harder and did not harm her. Why is she still in breach of the rules?
opts: Steroids are banned, whatever the effect on her
Steroids are only banned if they cause harm
Steroids are banned only at national events
Steroids are allowed if used to recover from training
b.why: Anabolic steroids are banned because they give an unfair advantage and risk health. Training harder and recovering faster is exactly the unfair advantage, so the lack of harm to Jess does not make her use allowed.
b.clue: Recall the two reasons steroids are on the banned list.
